item.title: More Questions Than Answers About the Israeli Mole Inside the UN
item.description: Two weeks since news broke that an Israeli mole working inside the United Nations was leaking confidential information years ago to Israeli diplomats, the organization has released few facts about the allegations against Yahav Lichner. That means there are more questions than answers right now. A Drop Site News investigation, published on Aug. 4, revealed ... Read more

item.title: Ebola: Motorbike riders carrying the sick may hold key to response boost
item.description: From the frontlines of the deadliest-ever Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the UN World Health Organization (WHO) shared details on Tuesday of a massive push for community engagement, a day after yet another ambulance attack.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Drone strikes and political impasse in Libya
item.description: The Security Council is meeting on Libya Tuesday as the country faces a political impasse delaying long-planned elections alongside heatwaves, tensions and violence, including drone strikes last week that left a major oil refinery ablaze. UN News app users can follow here.

item.title: Colombia earthquake: UN ramps up aid for 100,000 people
item.description: The UN is scaling up humanitarian assistance in western Colombia as needs continue to grow following last week’s devastating 7.4-magnitude earthquake, according to the latest update released on Tuesday.

item.title: Gaza: Only three per cent of cropland available to grow food
item.description: Amid ongoing deadly hostilities in Gaza, the enclave’s farmers face the increasingly difficult challenge of finding safe land to grow their crops.

item.title: Singapore: Independent rights experts urge immediate end to ‘unlawful use’ of death penalty
item.description: Independent UN Human Rights Council-appointed experts on Tuesday condemned the execution of at least 16 people in Singapore for drug-related offences this year and urged the country to end its “continued and unlawful use of capital punishment.”

item.title: What’s journalism worth in disasters and emergencies? A lot, says a new UN report
item.description: A single New York Times article on a disaster generated an additional $500,000 in official aid. That’s just one of the findings on the critical role a free press plays in saving lives, according to a new UN report released on Tuesday.

item.title: Lebanon: 860,000 displaced people have returned home, but humanitarian crisis remains ‘immense’
item.description: Around 860,000 people displaced by the conflict in southern Lebanon have returned, but the displacement and humanitarian crisis are “far from over,” the UN warned on Tuesday.

item.title: Indigenous Peoples Call for Meaningful Influence in Climate Discussions — Nia Tero

item.title: Nairobi Biodiversity Talks Set the Stage for Key COP17 Decisions
item.description: Despite record participation in global biodiversity reporting and planning processes, countries remain off track to meet the world’s 2030 biodiversity goals, according to discussions that concluded this month at two key meetings under the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
